why: Rule 1 outright: both prongs cool toward 13002 and p4 shows two different Bragg shapes away from it - a proton falling 260k from the 13000 end and a muon climbing to 160k at 13001 - and the zoom shows a real kink, not a collinear pair.

Only junction in a 16 cm event: the 13.5 cm track Braggs to 114k at 11001 so its other end is here, but the two prongs leave 11002 at about 154 degrees (collinearity trap) so this could be one scattered particle.

Rule 3 plus rule 1: the 217 cm muon is MIP 65k here and Braggs to 134k at 15000 where a 6.4 cm electron segment sits 6.6 cm off the stopping end (Michel, so that is the far end), and 15001 starts in the detector interior inside a halo of sub-cm fragments.
Rule 8 abstention: the whole event is two isolated sub-cm dots 150 cm apart with no fitted track, no dQ/dx panel and no readable direction, so any click is as good as any other.

Best rule-1 junction in a messy 36-vertex event: deg-3 with a heavily ionising 8.2 cm prong (109k rising to a 190k peak) stopping at 19001 and a 19.4 cm MIP prong stopping at 19000, both cooling toward 19002, while the rival cluster-80 tangle has prongs that are hotter at its junction.

Textbook two-Bragg junction: 2 of 2 prongs rise away, p4 gives a proton falling from 175k at 27000 and a muon climbing to 107k at 27001, and the zoom shows a roughly 90 degree kink in X-Z so it is not one scattered track.

Rule 1: the 32.5 cm muon cools to 14000 and Braggs to 130k at the far end 14002, and the hot 15 cm proton-like cluster-48 track begins 4.9 cm away at 48020, so the vertex is this muon-start/proton-start junction; 14000 carries the rise-away evidence while 48020 is flat.

Only degree-3 junction in a fragmented event and no prong is hotter at it: seg 6004 rises nearly ninefold away from 6003 to a 108k end at 6001 while the other two prongs are flat, whereas clusters 80 and 81 are plain all-flat two-prong bends.

Rule 1 plus geometry: the 63.6 cm heavily ionising track is coolest here (81k) and climbs to 116k as it exits at z=501, 19026 sits in the detector interior, and both EM tangles start 20-35 cm downstream of it like photon conversion gaps.

Rule 1 with 2 of 2 prongs rising away and two distinct Bragg shapes in p4 - a proton decaying from 265k at 14000 and a muon spiking to 190k at 14002 - which a single scattered particle cannot produce; chord angle 144 degrees stays under the collinearity flag.

The 233k end is a 7-8 cm plateau peaking well before the endpoint, not a muon Bragg (hot-blob trap), the muon's other end 7000 lies on the z=500 wall so it exits and is flat MIP for 67 cm, and the shower spray begins 13 cm from 7001 and runs about 110 cm, far too long for a Michel.
Rule 8 abstention: the event is two isolated sub-cm stubs at z=186 and z=496 with no fitted trajectory and no dQ/dx information, so there is nothing to read a direction from.

Rule 3 and rule 1 agree: the 43 cm muon cools toward 5001 and ends at 5002 in a four-prong stop whose only real prong is a 7.2 cm MIP electron (a Michel) plus junk stubs, and there is no genuine Bragg at 5001, only a single endpoint spike; 5001 is also the upstream end.

The 307 cm chain exits at the x=+200 anode at 26000 but ends in the interior at 26001 with no Bragg, so 26001 is a start, and it carries a 6.3 cm prong that climbs to 165k and stops at 26002 - a muon plus stopping proton vertex, lowest z of the chain with everything forward.
